reason: Frozen rubric A3: the updated object (shared reasoner/rubricator policy weights) and the rubric product are weights-side; rubrics are regenerated per rollout, used once as auxiliary reward or inference hint, and never persisted or reused as a prompt/skill/memory/evaluator artifact. This is weight training with a self-generated reward (SCORE_SPEC: weight-only training without retained non-weight change is out of scope). Dissent note for aggregator: domain card H24 lists rubric-as-reward members, so a boundary reading is possible; no score is given and the card is not edited.

paper.title: Reinforcing Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Self-Evolving Rubrics
paper.central_claim: RLCER rewards chain-of-thought with self-proposed rubrics, kept when their satisfaction correlates with final-answer correctness, and evolves the rubric generator by rewarding the fraction of valid rubrics, outperforming outcome-only RLVR and giving inference-time hints.

evidence.quote: which enhances the outcome-centric RLVR by rewarding CoTs with self-proposed and self-evolving rubrics.
evidence.support_explanation: Central contribution is a reward-shaping scheme inside RLVR weight training; the evaluated artifact is the trained policy.

evidence.quote: while their roles are distinguished by different prompts
evidence.support_explanation: Reasoner and rubricator are the same policy parameters under different prompts: the evolving "rubric generator" lives in weights.

evidence.quote: Gradients from both roles are aggregated to update the same set of parameters
evidence.support_explanation: The only state changed by feedback is the shared policy weights.

evidence.quote: Additionally, we encourage the rubricator to self-evolve its rubric generation capability by rewarding the fraction of valid rubrics among its proposals
evidence.support_explanation: Rubric evolution = RL on the rubricator role (a weight update), with a validity reward from outcome correlation.

evidence.quote: The rubrics generated under the rubricator role will then be used for judging the CoT quality through an external verifier
evidence.support_explanation: Rubrics are generated per (question, CoT) and consumed immediately by a frozen verifier; no rubric store, archive or version is described anywhere in the material.

evidence.quote: by performing supervised fine-tuning on correctly formatted data obtained via reject sampling from a stronger teacher model
evidence.support_explanation: Cold start uses a stronger teacher (Doubao-Seed-1.6-thinking) for reasoner and rubricator data and the verifier is distilled from it.

evidence.quote: training with RLCER outperforms the vanilla RLVR across multiple datasets and multiple model sizes on average.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline result (author-reported, single table, no variance).

evidence.quote: we explicitly employ these self-proposed rubrics as in-prompt hints, and evaluate the model’s reasoning performance under this setup.
evidence.support_explanation: The only non-weight use of rubrics is regenerated on the fly as inference hints; nothing is persisted or reused across tasks.

evidence.quote: our method is still quite limited to the RLVR domain, leaving the effectiveness of rewarding with self-proposed rubrics on non-verifiable domains unknown.
the introduction of the rubricator role increases the rollout burden and thereby requires more training time.

signatures.object: policy weights shared by reasoner and rubricator roles (PPO); transient per-sample rubrics are the intermediate product
signatures.information: question, CoT, ground-truth answer (for validity), frozen distilled verifier judging rubric satisfaction
signatures.operation: rubricator proposes rubrics per (question, CoT); a rubric is valid if its satisfaction correlates with answer correctness across 8 rollouts (threshold 0.2) and is discriminative; CoT reward = normalized score of satisfied valid rubrics; rubricator reward = fraction valid
signatures.output: role-specific rewards for a joint policy update
signatures.selection_rule: per-question validity filter (computed fresh each step)
signatures.persistence: not_applicable beyond weights: no rubric store, archive or version
signatures.later_use: none for rubrics except optional regenerated inference hints
signatures.claimed_effect: outperforms vanilla RLVR on average across 7 benchmarks for 4B/8B
signatures.failure_boundary: RLVR domain only; extra rollout cost
